stories.title: Dutch court hands life sentence to Rwandan man for genocide role
stories.summary:
A Dutch court has handed a life sentence to a Rwandan man for his role in the 1994 genocide. The defendant, identified as Eugene N., was convicted by a court in The Hague of war crimes and the crime of genocide.

The conviction relates to his participation in a massacre at a stadium where approximately 3,000 Tutsis were killed. At the time of sentencing, the man was 66 years old.

stories.title: Norway mourns King Harald as Haakon VIII ascends throne
stories.summary:
Norway has entered a period of mourning following the death of King Harald V at the age of 89. The monarch had led the country for 35 years before his passing.

His son, Haakon VIII, has ascended to the throne and adopted the family motto "all for Norway." Mourners, including royals, politicians, and citizens, gathered outside the palace to pay their respects.

The transition marks a new chapter for the Norwegian royal family, which has occasionally faced scandals during its tenure.

The removal of the mines has opened the critical waterway to growing commercial traffic following a period of heightened tension in the region.

President Donald Trump stated that this dramatic shift in military and economic pressure has left Iran “begging to make a deal.”

The Washington Times reported that the commander of U.S. Central Command specifically noted that all sea mines spread along the maritime transit routes have been successfully cleared.

The group pulled cardboard over themselves and intended to stay awake, but they eventually fell asleep. By morning, one of the boys had died.

Spencer had been known to police and child protection services for several years prior to his death.

stories.title: Pentagon’s blacklisting of Anthropic was unlawful, US judge rules
stories.summary:
A US federal judge ruled on Thursday that the Pentagon’s designation of Anthropic as a supply chain risk was unlawful. The court found that the Trump administration broke the law by targeting the AI firm for refusing to comply with defense department demands.

The ruling marks a significant legal victory for Anthropic, which argued that the blacklist could cost billions in lost business and reputational harm. The judge stated that an empty invocation of national security is not a blank check to punish or retaliate against government contractors.

This decision comes as a second lawsuit between Anthropic and the Pentagon continues in Washington. The verdict highlights ongoing tensions between federal agencies and private AI developers regarding compliance with defense sector requirements.

stories.title: Nicola Coughlan and Matt Lucas among stars backing campaign against AI voice cloning
stories.summary:
A group of prominent British actors has launched a campaign to combat the unauthorized use of artificial intelligence for voice cloning. The initiative, titled Save Our Voices Now, seeks to prevent AI technology from replicating real people's voices without consent.

The movement is backed by high-profile figures including Nicola Coughlan, Matt Lucas, and Hugh Bonneville. Other supporters include Luke Evans, Jen Brister, Siobhán McSweeney, and Pearl Mackie.

Approximately 80 individuals have signed an open letter addressed to Andy Burnham. The signatories are calling for new legislation that would explicitly protect voice ownership rights.

stories.title: Enhanced habagat to bring rains over western Luzon – Pagasa
stories.summary:
The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) warned that a low-pressure area off Extreme Northern Luzon will persist through Saturday, August 29. This system is expected to enhance the southwest monsoon, or habagat, resulting in rains over western Luzon.

Weather specialist Loriedin Dela Cruz-Galicia confirmed the forecast during an update on the developing weather conditions. The enhanced monsoon activity has prompted local authorities to take precautionary measures across affected regions.

In response to the heavy rainfall, class suspensions have been implemented for Saturday in various areas. Rappler reported a list of locations where schools are closed due to the impact of the enhanced southwest monsoon.

The six-page case information was submitted to the anti-graft court for one count of malversation each. This legal action follows previous corruption cases involving Co, who is currently a fugitive from justice.

stories.title: Manila Water advances complete water cycle management with September desludging
stories.summary:
Manila Water has launched a September desludging program to strengthen its wastewater management initiatives. The utility aims to advance complete water cycle management by integrating this preventive sanitation service with its ongoing efforts to develop new water sources and expand treatment capacity.

Customers across the East Zone are encouraged to participate in the program, which is designed to help ensure effective sanitation. This initiative complements Manila Water's broader goals of improving distribution infrastructure while maintaining robust wastewater handling systems.

stories.title: Tacloban City mayor, NBI tackle tighter safety, security measures
stories.summary:
Tacloban City Mayor Alfred Romualdez met with the newly assigned National Bureau of Investigation Region 8 Director, Atty. Jeremy Lotoc, to discuss enhanced safety and security protocols.

The meeting focused on implementing stricter measures for responsible firearm ownership and improving cybersecurity within government agencies.

Romualdez, who serves as chair of the Regional Peace and Order Council, specifically raised concerns regarding unauthorized access to firearms during the discussion.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and 100 other companies call for action to defend against rogue AI
stories.summary:
Major technology firms including OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google have joined over 100 other companies in a collective call for action against emerging AI-driven cyber threats.

The coalition aims to address what it describes as the current state of cybersecurity, which they argue is insufficient to handle new generations of digital risks.

By uniting large tech giants with AI startups, the group seeks to promote a new solution designed specifically to defend against rogue artificial intelligence systems.

stories.title: AI can detect heart disease in women using mammograms, study suggests
stories.summary:
Researchers have demonstrated that artificial intelligence can identify signs of heart disease in women by analyzing routine mammograms. The study suggests that breast cancer screenings could simultaneously flag cardiovascular issues, which are a leading cause of death for women but often underdiagnosed.

The AI system was able to successfully detect coronary heart disease, high blood pressure, and previous strokes from the scans. Experts indicate that this dual-purpose approach could enhance early detection efforts during standard medical procedures.

stories.title: AI-proof? Younger workers desert the digital world for traditional crafts
stories.summary:
Younger workers are increasingly turning away from digital careers and toward traditional heritage crafts as the job market becomes more disrupted. The shift includes trades such as bookbinding, metalwork, and boatbuilding.

This trend reflects a bleak moment for first-time entrants to the workforce who previously relied on university degrees to secure stable employment. Entry-level white-collar jobs across almost all sectors are no longer seen as reliable guarantees of career stability.

stories.title: Black Box: The Chatbots: a new series from The Guardian Investigates – trailer
stories.summary:
The Guardian Investigates has announced a new audio series titled "Black Box: The Chatbots."

The upcoming production explores the widespread belief that artificial intelligence chatbots have contributed to significant scientific breakthroughs.

Reporters will examine how these tools are credited with helping users cure diseases and invent new technologies.

The series aims to analyze what this perception reveals about a technology now used by more than one billion people.
